name: Maryland
overview: Maryland sells liens, not property: when real property taxes are in arrears, the tax collector of each county (and Baltimore City) must offer the property at a tax sale, and the buyer receives a certificate of sale. Each county runs its own sale and sets its own date and bidding rules, so check the county entries below. The owner can redeem by paying the sale amount plus interest, which state law sets at 6% a year unless a county fixes its own rate by local law. The certificate holder may file to foreclose the right of redemption 6 months after the sale (9 months for owner-occupied homes), and the certificate is void unless foreclosure is filed within 2 years.

platform.name: Prince George's County tax sale website

counties.next_sale_note: 2027 date not yet posted. The 2026 online sale is over (bidding opened May 4, 2026; accounts awarded May 11, 2026), and unsold county-held certificates were offered by email from June 10, 2026.
counties.how_to_bid: Per the 2026 Bidding Rules: an Internet-based sealed direct-bid auction using the high-bid premium method, not a live in-person auction. Bidders register on the county tax sale website (no mail-in or email registration), upload an IRS W-9, and pay a non-refundable $150 registration fee and a $1,000 deposit by ACH debit. Bids are entered on the website as a dollar amount or a bid factor; payment is by wire or cashier's check by 3:00 p.m. the day after the sale. Interest: 10% per year for owner-occupied property, 20% for other property.

counties.schedule_rule: The tax sale is held annually online via the Real Auction website.
counties.next_sale_note: 2027 date not yet posted. The county FAQ gives registration and bidding days (May and early June) without a year.
counties.how_to_bid: Per the county FAQ: bidding is online through the Real Auction website, linked from the FAQ as the county's official tax certificate auction site. There is a $100 nonrefundable bidder registration fee. The taxes, interest and fees are due by 4 pm on the day of the sale via ACH, plus any bid premium; the balance of the bid is due on foreclosure. The county uses the bid premium method: if a bid exceeds 40% of the property's full cash value, the bidder pays a 20% premium on the excess, returned without interest if the certificate is redeemed or foreclosed within 2 years. Unsold liens may be bought over the counter.
